perf.summary: Hoist (int)w[i], w[i], v[i] out of both branches' inner loops and hoist (int)tw out of the binary-split inner loop.
perf.currentCost: In the unbounded branch 'dp[j - (int)w[i]] + v[i]' re-reads w[i] (with a long->int cast) and v[i] every iteration. In the bounded branch 'dp[j - (int)tw]' casts tw to int each j. The class name says DivideConquer but the body is plain binary-splitting; no D&C optimization is present.
perf.proposedChange: At top of the i-loop read 'int wi = (int)w[i]; long vi = v[i];'. Unbounded branch: 'for (int j = wi; j <= cap; j++) { long cand = dp[j - wi] + vi; ... }'. Bounded branch: hoist 'int itw = (int)tw;' before the inner for and use dp[j - itw].
perf.rationale: Removes a per-iteration long->int narrowing and two long loads from each inner-loop body, the dominant O(cap) cost. Identical to the BoundedKnapsack hoist; shortens the load-add-compare-store chain.
perf.risk: None: w[i]/v[i] are invariant across j; the cast result is invariant. Same outputs.
